advances: An ordinary simplex section inequality with exactly four active heights and arbitrary zero heights.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
By affine equivalence use the barycentric simplex. With independent unit exponentials $Y_i$, the sign of the raw form on the uniform simplex agrees with the sign of $V=\sum_i c_iY_i$, since $Y/\sum_iY_i$ is uniform. The coarea means $\mu_i=\mathbb E[Y_i\mid V=0]$ are $db_i$ by 6df0487380ed701a. In its eliminated-coordinate density, take an active eliminated coordinate. Each zero-height variable then factors as a unit exponential, independently of the active conditional coordinates. Therefore it has mean one, and deleting all such variables preserves the active means and $F$. Apply the same relation in the remaining tetrahedron: its section centroid $b^*$ satisfies $\mu_i=3b_i^*$ on the active indices. An active omission is now covered by the strict quadrilateral case of ae5fd0716d158534.

Write the four active heights as $(p,q,-r,-s)$ with all magnitudes positive, and set
$$
D=pq(r+s)+rs(p+q),\qquad K=(p+r)(p+s)(q+r)(q+s),\qquad \theta=\frac{ps(q+r)}D .
$$
The accepted raw formulas in 1462fa9ce6ced54e give $\theta=\alpha/(\alpha+\delta)$ and, by inserting the four listed edge intersections,
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mu_0&=\frac r{p+r}+\frac{\theta s}{p+s},&
\mu_1&=\frac s{q+s}+\frac{(1-\theta)r}{q+r},\\
\mu_2&=\frac p{p+r}+\frac{(1-\theta)q}{q+r},&
\mu_3&=\frac q{q+s}+\frac{\theta p}{p+s},\\
F&=\frac{p^2q^2+pq(p+q)(r+s)+rs(p^2+pq+q^2)}K .
\end{aligned}
$$
All these denominators are positive, including at repeated heights. For $a\ge b$ set $M_{ab}(u,v)=u^av^b+\mathbf1_{\{a>b\}}u^bv^a$. Define $S_{ab,cd}=M_{ab}(p,q)M_{cd}(r,s)+M_{cd}(p,q)M_{ab}(r,s)$ when $(a,b)\ne(c,d)$, and use only the first summand when the pairs agree. With the formulas above, multiplication and collection gives
$$
K^2D^4\left(\prod_{i=0}^3\mu_i-F(1-F)\right)=\sum_{ab,cd} C_{ab,cd} S_{ab,cd},
$$
with the following nonzero entries:
$$
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrrr}
(ab,cd)&(77,60)&(77,51)&(77,42)&(77,33)&(76,61)&(76,52)&(76,43)&(75,62)\\
C&1&4&7&9&5&17&28&10\\
(ab,cd)&(75,53)&(75,44)&(74,63)&(74,54)&(73,64)&(73,55)&(72,65)&(66,62)\\
C&29&40&10&24&5&9&1&24\\
(ab,cd)&(66,53)&(66,44)&(65,63)&(65,54)&(64,64)&(64,55)&(55,55)&\\
C&76&104&53&134&68&118&210&
\end{array}
$$
For direct verification, the four numerator factors of the product, after clearing its common denominator $K^2D^4$, are
$$
\begin{aligned}
&r(p+s)D+s(p+r)ps(q+r),\\
&s(q+r)D+r(q+s)qr(p+s),\\
&p(q+r)D+q(p+r)qr(p+s),\\
&q(p+s)D+p(q+s)ps(q+r).
\end{aligned}
$$
From their product subtract $D^4A(K-A)$, where $A$ is the displayed numerator of $F$, and collect the four-variable monomials as specified by $S_{ab,cd}$. The resulting polynomial has the listed 23 positive entries and 129 positive monomials upon expansion. Hence the product of all four active means strictly exceeds $F(1-F)$. This is precisely the product after omitting an inactive coordinate because all other inactive means equal one.

source_sections.locator: 628a958af5b83522:03 Opening (1), §3, (2)–(3), exactly two positive and two negative phases

statement:
Let a proper cut of a $d$-simplex have exactly two positive and two negative raw vertex heights, with all other heights zero. Let $F$ be the relative volume of either cap and $b$ the barycentric centroid of the actual uniform section. Then for every omitted vertex index $j$,
$$
F(1-F)<d^d\prod_{i\ne j} b_i .
$$
The product of the four active numbers $d b_i$ itself also strictly exceeds $F(1-F)$.
title: Cap variance with two positive and two negative simplex heights and arbitrary zeros
